subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow core agent-meeting lifecycle primitive now, and if so what storage, authorization, transcript-retention, and handoff-layer shape should it use?
rationale: The current code has usable lower-level delivery/session primitives and the docs reserve the `meet` namespace, but the proposed core verbs would create durable cross-agent state and security-sensitive transcript behavior that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
options.body: Define the MVP as `meet`/teleconference lifecycle verbs over existing delivery/session primitives with explicit SQLite-or-product-artifact storage, auth, retention, and tests before inviting an implementation PR.

options.title: Route to plugin first
options.body: Ask for the prototype to ship as a plugin or ClawHub package until a missing core API is demonstrated, keeping core lean while preserving the experiment.

options.title: Defer under the broader multi-agent RFC
options.body: Close or pause this narrow direction in favor of the broader multi-agent collaboration roadmap if maintainers want one architectural decision surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core design
recommendation.body: Define the MVP as `meet`/teleconference lifecycle verbs over existing delivery/session primitives with explicit SQLite-or-product-artifact storage, auth, retention, and tests before inviting an implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the item-specific scoping review and has recent history in the session/A2A and VISION policy surfaces that govern this decision.
